result.reasoning:
REFUTED. The op-level arithmetic the reporter shows is real, but it only appears for an input convention the production store does not use, and on the production store the screen measurably does the opposite of what the report claims.

1) What I could reproduce, and what I could not.
Reproduced (ops_ext.py:277, 365): a day with 1 finite minute carrying Ret=+0.01 gives day_zero_ratio = 0.0000; 241 finite minutes of Ret=0 gives 1.0000. So the report's [B] numbers are right as arithmetic. NOT reproduced: the consequence. The value 0.0 needs TWO things at once — (a) the no-trade minutes must be ABSENT (NaN), and (b) every one of the few surviving minutes must carry a non-zero Ret. Both fail on the real store.

2) (a) fails: in the production store a no-trade minute's bar exists and its return is a finite 0, so a thin day reads as near-maximally frozen, not minimally.
The repo's own measurements on the real store say the bars are dense, not sparse:
- /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/docs/new_operators.md:28 defines day_zero_ratio(Ret) as "Ret 在 0 上的点质量(封板 / 停牌 / 无成交的分钟)" — no-trade minutes are counted IN the zero mass, i.e. they are finite zeros.
- /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/research/alpha_distillation/F101_day_shine_retstd.md:170 (a probe run on the real store): "全天无成交的行 ΔVolume 恒为 0" — a stock-day with no trades at all still has finite Volume=0 on every minute. Bars are present.
- lab/findings.yaml f10x (in_pct): "零 / 近零成交分钟把它炸成极端重尾" — in_pct's denominator is blown up BY zero-volume minutes, which requires them to be finite 0, not NaN.
- lab/findings.yaml:129: "任何「日内收益类统计量 == 0」的格子都是一字板日" — a fully locked day gives day stats of exactly 0, which requires 241 finite zero returns, not NaN.
My [A] script prints what the op then returns for a thin day under each convention (241 nominal minutes, k traded minutes):
  dense bars (no-trade Ret=0): k=1 -> zero_ratio 0.9959; k=2 -> 0.9917; k=40 -> ~0.83 (vs a liquid tick-grid day at ~0.13)
  sparse NaN + non-zero Ret (the report's input): 0.0000
  sparse NaN but the bar's own open->close return (a single-trade bar has open==close): 1.0000
Under the only two conventions consistent with the store, a thin name sits at the TOP of x, exactly where cs_last_high20 throws it out.

3) (b) fails too, even if one assumes sparse bars. For x = cross_max(day_zero_ratio(Ret),15) to be 0 the stock needs FIFTEEN CONSECUTIVE days with not one minute whose Ret is exactly 0. A-share thin names re-print the same tick constantly. With consecutive trade prices on a 1-tick lattice (50% re-prints), P(no exact-zero return in a day) is 0.26 at k=2 and 0.03 at k=5, so P(x=0 for 15 days running) is 1e-9 / 1e-23. My [B] run includes this case ("sparse_tick_k40"): x = 0.59-0.63, screened 100% of days, held 0%.

4) End-to-end, through the real engine and the real book. [B] builds a synthetic cube with thin names injected under each convention, evaluates the headline expression with CubeEngine, and forms the top-decile book with alphacube.metrics.long_short_weights + partura.books.smoothed(hl=2). Result: the thin names are held 100% of days ONLY in the sparseNaN groups; in the dense groups (k=2 and k=40) and the sparse-barret and sparse-tick groups they are screened out on 100% of days and held 0% — even though their y rank (neg(cross_mean(day_std(Amt),30))) is 0.82-0.99, i.e. y does love them exactly as the report says. The screen catches them anyway.

5) The decisive check: the production-store anatomies already on disk measure the premise directly, and they contradict it. [C] pulls every anatomy signal that carries the cross_max(day_zero_ratio(Ret),15) screen and compares its book composition with unscreened k_known = cross_mean(day_std(Amt),30):
  成交额(20日):最低20%  held 0.9990 -> 0.6109 mean over 20 screened variants (h_K_ex_both itself: 0.7894), in-segment annual excess -4.14% -> +4.90% (h_K_ex_both: +8.19%)
  成交额(20日):20-40%  held 0.0010 -> 0.2985  (the displaced weight goes to the next quintile up)
  近15日有冻结盘口      held 0.0356 -> 0.0107
The screen displaces 21-39 pp of the THINNEST turnover quintile out of the book and flips that quintile's in-segment excess from negative to positive. That is arithmetically impossible if the thinnest names were sitting at x = 0 and surviving the cut: names removed by a top-20%-of-x cut must have HIGH x, and they are concentrated in the lowest-turnover quintile. So on real data day_zero_ratio(Ret) is high for thin names, the screen fires on them, and "筛子恰好在它要防的那批票上失效" is false. k_known_xfrozen (+18.54%) and h_K_ex_both (+18.10% / holdout +16.78%) are not inflated by this mechanism.

6) Residual, reported as a non-finding: the guard really is only n>0 / n>1, so IF the store ever switched to sparse minute bars (a vendor change, or a partial-day halt that truncates the row), a day with very few finite minutes would read 0.0. Today that costs nothing — with 241 finite minutes per tradable stock-day, a "n >= 30" guard is a no-op. The op also matches its own docstring ("share of the day's FINITE minutes with x == 0"), so there is no definition/implementation mismatch to fix.

result.corrected_fix:
Not needed today — but if the team wants the guard anyway as insurance against a future sparse-bar store, two of the three suggested changes are wrong and should not be made:

1. "分母换成当天的名义分钟数 T 而不是有限分钟数" — do not. On the current dense store T == n, so it changes nothing; on a suspended day it would turn today's clean NaN into 0/241 = 0.0, i.e. it would make a suspended stock read as the LEAST frozen name in the cross-section. That introduces the exact bug the report is worried about.

2. "n >= 30 或 n >= 0.5*T 否则返回 NaN" — harmless but not free. Today it is a no-op (241 finite minutes per tradable stock-day). On any stock-day that IS truncated (a resumption day, an intraday halt, a listing day), NaN-ing x does not merely exclude the name: cs_last_high20/_lexi require isfinite(x), so the name drops out of the signal entirely that day, silently shrinking the universe and moving the benchmark (long_book's ew is taken over names with both signal and label). If it is added, it must be added with a measurement of how many stock-days it NaN-s and a re-run of the k_known_xfrozen / h_K_ex_both rows, not as a quiet hardening.

3. The documentation half of the suggestion is the only part worth doing: say in docs/new_operators.md that the denominator is the day's FINITE minutes and that this is safe only because the production store carries dense bars (a no-trade minute is a finite Ret = 0). That records the data assumption the op depends on, so a vendor/store change gets caught.
